2609.04159.title: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center
2609.04159.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous SOC analysts, but two limitations make them unreliable at enterprise scale: a finite context window cannot hold a multi-thousand-host authentication graph, and free-form generation offers no guarantee that a recommended containment action is consistent with the topology it operates on. We present Sentinel-RL, an agentic-SOC architecture that decouples topological reasoning from semantic reasoning: a heterogeneous graph attention encoder summarizes the live authentication subgraph into a fixed-dimensional state, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy maps this state to a constrained set of investigative actions, and an LLM agent loop is restricted to consuming the policy's recommendations and producing analyst-readable narratives gated by a critic. We instantiate the system on the LANL Comprehensive, Multi-Source Cyber-Security Events dataset and the Indiana University Quartz HPC cluster, reporting four results: (i) a two-phase CREATE ingestion pattern loads a 24M-edge authentication subgraph into Neo4j in 14.2 minutes on a single 32-core node, roughly 24x faster than the canonical MERGE-based pipeline; (ii) a sliding-window alert engine reliably trips a 25-event/10-second threshold in <=2.5 s across 50 trials; (iii) PPO training over 200 iterations converges to a mean episodic return of 8.74+/-0.31, with held-out precision of 0.91 and recall of 0.87 on labeled red-team events; and (iv) the integrated containment loop completes a full detect-investigate-recommend-human-approve cycle in a median of 6.3 s. We contribute a reusable engineering pattern (the hot-node deadlock workaround), a portable HPC deployment pattern (anchor-node co-location), and an enterprise-readiness analysis covering false-positive economics, reversibility guarantees, audit compliance, and the human-approval boundary.
2609.04159.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）代理被越來越多地提議作為自主的安全運營中心（SOC）分析師，但有兩個限制使其在企業規模上不可靠：有限的上下文窗口無法容納數千主機的身份驗證圖，而自由形式生成無法保證建議的遏制行動與其操作的拓撲一致。我們提出了 Sentinel-RL，一種將拓撲推理與語義推理解耦的代理SOC架構：一個異質圖注意力編碼器將實時身份驗證子圖總結為固定維度的狀態，一個近端策略優化（PPO）策略將此狀態映射到一組受限的調查行動，而LLM代理循環僅限於消耗該策略的建議並生成由批評者控制的分析師可讀敘述。我們在LANL綜合多源網絡安全事件數據集和印第安納大學Quartz HPC集群上實現了該系統，報告了四個結果：（i）一種兩階段的CREATE攝取模式在單個32核節點上將2400萬邊的身份驗證子圖加載到Neo4j中，耗時14.2分鐘，速度約為經典MERGE基礎管道的24倍；（ii）滑動窗口警報引擎在50次試驗中可靠地在<=2.5秒內觸發25事件/10秒的閾值；（iii）在200次迭代中，PPO訓練收斂到均值回報8.74+/-0.31，對標記的紅隊事件的保留精度為0.91，召回率為0.87；（iv）集成的遏制循環在中位數6.3秒內完成完整的檢測-調查-建議-人類批准循環。我們貢獻了一個可重用的工程模式（熱節點死鎖解決方法）、一個可攜式HPC部署模式（錨節點共置），以及一個涵蓋假陽性經濟學、可逆性保證、審計合規性和人類批准邊界的企業準備分析。
